exercise.name: Suitcase Carry
library_steps: Hold one heavy dumbbell at your side, other arm free.
Walk tall without leaning toward the weight.
Set it down, then carry it the same distance in the other hand.
exercise.one_line_summary: Walking tall with one heavy dumbbell hanging in the left hand and the right arm free; the trunk stays upright and level instead of leaning toward the weight. Picture 1: left foot forward; picture 2: right foot forward.

setup.target: One dumbbell in one hand (left in the pictures), arm straight at the side, palm in.
Tall and level: shoulders level, no lean toward or away from the weight.
setup.why: The side opposite the load must hold the trunk up; that is the training effect (S2).

setup.target: Right arm hanging relaxed, a little away from the side.

movement.start: ankle 0.15 m in front of the hip, foot flat, knee ~13 deg
ankle 0.17 m behind the hip, heel up ~15 deg, knee ~36 deg

movement.tolerance: under 5 deg; peak lateral bend in S1 one-hand carries was small (~5 deg)

muscles.emg: 30 kg in the right hand: left external oblique 47.3 % MVC, left internal oblique 32.5 % vs 3.9 % / 6.1 % with 15 kg in each hand (S2)
muscles.role: Hold the trunk upright against the one-sided pull; what the exercise is for. (The mask lights both sides.)
muscles.surface: Side of the waist between ribs and hip bone.

muscles.emg: Left rectus 26.0 % MVC at 30 kg in the right hand (S2), 55 % of the top oblique

muscles.role: Keeps the loaded shoulder from being pulled down; library secondary.

muscles.emg: Modelled (S1); with the lateral abdominal wall it holds the pelvis level (S1, S2 discussion)
Left lumbar ES 25.3 % MVC at 30 kg right-hand carry (S2)
muscles.surface: Either side of the lower spine.

muscles.role: Holds the pelvis level on the stance leg.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Loaded shoulder drops, trunk bends to that side.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library step 2; the trunk muscles stop working against the load.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far away / hiking the free arm out
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Trunk tips away, free arm held out wide.

sources.citation: McGill SM, McDermott A, Fenwick CMJ. 2009. Comparison of different strongman events: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res 23(4):1148-1161.
sources.what_it_gave: Left- and right-hand suitcase carries (~37-42 kg bar): trunk EMG, spine motion (small lateral bend, larger twist with a waddling gait); quadratus lumborum and abdominal wall hold the pelvis.

sources.citation: McGill SM, Marshall L, Andersen J. 2013. Low back loads while walking and carrying: comparing the load carried in one hand or in both hands. Ergonomics 56(2):293-302.
sources.what_it_gave: Table 3: one-hand 30 kg vs both-hands 15+15 kg EMG; opposite-side external oblique 47.3 vs 3.9 % MVC; L4/L5 compression 2874 vs 1628 N.

sources.citation: McCall P. 2014. Strongman training for your clients. ACE ProSource.
sources.what_it_gave: Suitcase carry = heavy weight on one side, walked a set distance; internal oblique, quadratus lumborum, gluteus medius stabilise the pelvis.

clip_check.check: Shoulders level, no side-bend toward the dumbbell
Only the left hand holds a dumbbell; right hand open/relaxed
Front foot flat, back foot on its ball
Obliques are the strongest red in both pictures
